A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Omni-View and retain matching methods, equations, benchmarks, and main result tables. All pages and appendices are readable, supporting a reliable comparison despite the expanded appendix in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original scene-understanding, spatial-reasoning, and generation results in Tables 1–3, ablations in Tables 4–7, and qualitative appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds qualitative comparisons, scale-consistency examples, training-loss curves, activation visualizations, and inference timings.

M1.justification: Appendix A.5 introduces a generation variant that packs four consecutive views into one grid and generates grids autoregressively; B.4 identifies its use in stage 2. This locally modifies generation while retaining the three-module architecture, losses, and principal training recipe.

E1.justification: V2 adds targeted cross-scale, reference-conditioned depth-prediction examples from SPAR-7M, illustrated using Structured3D and ScanNet++ scenes (A.3), and explicit outdoor generation and depth-estimation scenarios (A.4). The training mixture and main benchmark coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–3 remain identical. Figure 3 adds a direct comparison of grid generation against the original frame-by-frame procedure, whose corresponding output was only a standalone failure example in v1. The activation comparison reuses BAGEL-FT.

E3.justification: New qualitative generation demonstrations extend through View-48, beyond v1's displayed View-24 examples, and Figure 3 compares grid and framewise configurations. Main quantitative evaluation settings remain unchanged. Appendix B's filtering rules and training budgets are newly disclosed details, not evidence that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining all original ablations, v2 adds analyses of scale consistency, grid generation versus framewise generation, indoor/outdoor depth quality and failures, training convergence, and BAGEL-FT versus Omni-View activations (A.3–A.5, B.4–B.5). These substantially broaden the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added raw and exponentially smoothed training-loss curves do not provide uncertainty estimates across runs.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 remain unchanged, including the 55.4 VSI-Bench average. V2 adds supplementary outcomes: depth predictions such as 2.0 meters against 2.2 meters ground truth, grid-consistency examples, outdoor failures, loss and activation patterns, and inference timings. These extend the results without changing benchmark rankings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same mathematical content; changes to module-name typography are cosmetic. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new appendices add no substantive theoretical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that generation facilitates 3D understanding, that the texture/geometry decomposition enables a unified model, and that Omni-View achieves 55.4 on VSI-Bench. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds specific qualifications about outdoor scenes with substantial camera movement, hypotheses connecting camera-loss spikes to learnable-query optimization, and broader attention as a possible explanation for improved understanding. It also suggests reducing the geometry-loss weight for stability. The original limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix B documents filtering rules, tokenizer and backbone details, parameter sizes, packed sequence lengths, 10,000/20,000 training iterations, and 32-H100 training costs. It also reports inference timings. The abstract now provides a repository and states that code and models are released, although the reproducibility statement still promises future release.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds three Hu et al. image-restoration references alongside a short extension from inpainting to restoration. The broader positioning relative to unified models and 3D understanding/generation work is retained; MV-AR's changed citation suffix identifies the same work.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely verbatim, with limited wording, affiliation, header, and cross-reference edits. The appendix is expanded and organized into additional qualitative and technical subsections, and the existing LLM-use disclosure becomes Appendix C.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands visual presentation with Figures 2–6, additional qualitative panels, architecture diagrams, and seven training-loss plots. The original NVS failure sequence is reused within Figure 3, while the original successful example is replaced. Tables are repositioned, and Table 3 gains explicit best/second-best highlighting.

improvement.justification: Appendix B makes implementation and computational requirements substantially easier to assess, while the new diagnostics clarify consistency failures and applicability boundaries. The grid comparison also directly revisits v1's failure example. The overall gain is limited by the largely illustrative nature of the added validation: benchmark evidence is unchanged, grid benefits are not quantified, and release-status wording remains inconsistent.
